# refine-cycle

**[Flow map](FLOW.md)** shows every agent, gate, loop and terminal state, generated by running the engine.

refine reviews one plan file before [develop](../develop/) builds it. It checks every `todo` block
against the real code and stops after one round that finds nothing. It changes only the plan file and
never writes code.

## How it works

Two agents take turns for up to `maxRounds` critic rounds. The last round is a confirm round. Its critic
runs and no editor follows, so a run that spends its budget ends on a critic. Each run writes its
critique files to its own launch folder, so every critique file is kept. The launch folder also holds a
copy of the plan as it was before the run.

1. A **critic** reads the repo and judges each `todo` block. It writes every gap it finds, with file and
   line evidence, to a critique file for that round. A round that finds nothing writes `No gaps.` to
   that file.
2. An **editor** checks each gap against the plan and the code. It takes the critic's change as a hint
   and writes its own correction, the smallest edit that closes the defect. It removes wrong method
   text, which says how to build, and never rewrites it. It corrects wrong requirement text in place.
   It declines a gap only when the defect is not real or only an addition or new method text would
   close it, and records the reason in `DISMISSED-PLAN.md`. When the correction is your choice to make,
   it asks you and the run ends. Then it checks that the plan still parses.

A plan review that keeps adding detail never ends. Four rules make this one finish.

- **Defects only.** A gap names plan text that is wrong, such as a contradiction, an instruction that
  builds broken code, a prescribed bad practice, or a wrong block order.
  A missing detail, an improvement, an alternative or a style choice is not a gap.
- **A severity floor.** Gaps below `critiqueSeverity` (default `major`) are never folded and count for
  nothing.
- **A dismissal ledger.** A declined gap stays declined. The critic may contest one once.
- **A minimal editor.** The editor checks each gap before folding it. It changes nothing a gap does not
  name.

## Results

- `converged` means the last round found no gap or question. The plan is ready for your approval.
  When that round has FYI items, it writes them as an FYI section in the last critique file.
  `belowFloor` counts them. No editor folds those items, so read the section with the plan. It has a
  subsection for each block with findings below the severity floor. A `File preamble` subsection holds
  findings in plan text above the first block, other than the file keys, and file-key findings below
  the floor. An `Outside the plan` subsection holds defects that no plan text holds. They sit in files
  the critic read to judge the plan. Items are numbered F1, F2 and so on. You can add an item to a block
  before you approve.
- `needs-answers` means the critic or the editor raised something only you can decide, such as a block
  order. Read `NEEDS-USER.md`, change the plan, and run refine again. When you keep the plan text, add
  your ruling to `DISMISSED-PLAN.md` as a `USER-RULED:` line instead. `NEEDS-USER.md` keeps the entries
  of earlier runs, so the newest entries are at its end. Each entry opens with its launch, its round and
  the agent that wrote it, such as `## launch 3 r2 critic`, and `nextStep` names the launch and round of
  the new entries.
- `dismissal-contested` means the critic contested a gap the editor had declined, and the editor passed
  it to you. Read the newest entries at the end of `NEEDS-USER.md`. Fold the gap into the plan, or add
  your ruling to `DISMISSED-PLAN.md` as a `USER-RULED:` line, which no later critic contests. Then run
  refine again.
- `rounds-exhausted` means the confirm round still found gaps. They are open in the plan, and the last
  critique file lists them. Rule on each gap: leave it for the next run to fold, add a `USER-RULED:` line
  to `DISMISSED-PLAN.md` to decline it, or edit the plan yourself. Then run refine again.
- A `BLOCKED` result names what stopped it and how to repair it.

## How to use it

- **Skill:** `/aipg:refine <path to the plan file>`
- **Plain pointer:** tell Claude to use the refine workflow in `aipg/workflows/refine/` on the plan.

Read `DISMISSED-PLAN.md` before you approve a converged plan, since each declined gap is a judgment call.

Ask for an [exit survey](../../README.md#exit-survey) to have each agent of the run report on the workflow.

## Requirements

- **Claude Code** with the background **Workflow** capability.
- The plan file, stored outside the target repo, and the target git repo it builds in.
